review.notes: Difference (2) could not be settled and drives the escalation flag: aux.CheckStealEquip lives in the modern cards_specific_functions.lua and may simply post-date the variant, in which case the face-down allowance is an artefact rather than a period reconstruction - but the shipped implementation does behave differently, and the helper also carries Trap Monster Spell & Trap Zone accounting that the period rule profile handles globally, so the two layers overlap. Only difference (1) is annotated by upstream. Everything else in the diff is spelling: EVENT_PHASE|PHASE_STANDBY vs EVENT_PHASE+PHASE_STANDBY, SET_ARCHFIEND vs 0x45, and Duel.IsTurnPlayer(1-tp) vs tp~=Duel.GetTurnPlayer(), which are the same tests. The chain starts at v1 (DR1-EN250, 2005-03-19), which the variant carries verbatim; earlier v0 (DCR-088, 2003-12-01) required a 'face-up Archfiend card' and 'face-up' opponent monsters and predates the baseline - interestingly it is v0, not v1, that matches the modern script's face-up requirement. Trailing v1 -> v2 (AP03-EN006, 2013-09-13) is PSCT that spells out equip targeting both scripts already perform through aux.AddEquipProcedure's EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET, so it is cosmetic and is recorded here rather than as a change entry.

event.historical_text: Destroy this card if there is no Archfiend card on your side of the field. Take control of 1 of your opponent's monsters that is equipped with this card. You take 800 points of damage during each of your opponent's Standby Phases.
event.summary: Two script-only differences, neither visible in any printed text. (1) The Standby Phase damage is conditional in the era version: the GOAT damcon adds 'not e:GetHandler():GetEquipTarget():IsImmuneToEffect(e)', so no 800 damage occurs while the equipped monster is immune to Falling Down's effect, where the modern damcon only checks the turn player - upstream annotates this 'If monster is immuned, no damage occurs'. (2) The equip/steal legality filter differs: the modern script passes aux.CheckStealEquip to aux.AddEquipProcedure, which requires the opponent's monster to be face-up and to have changeable control and, for Trap Monsters, Spell & Trap Zone room; the GOAT script passes Card.IsControlerCanBeChanged alone, so it will equip to and take control of a face-down opponent monster. Chronology of both is unresolved.
